chunks: So al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me, saying: Ja‘far ibn Muhammad informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from ‘Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his brother Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘, from Abi al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, who said:
“Allah the Exalted has made it obligatory upon women in wudu (ablution) that they begin with the inner side of their arms, and upon men with the outer side of the arm.”

Then al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: And it is permitted for a woman, regarding wiping her head, to wipe with one finger whatever part of it is connected to it, and to insert her finger beneath her head-covering and wipe over her hair, even if that is the measure of a fingertip, in the salat of zuhr, ‘asr, and the later ‘isha’; and she removes her head-covering in salat al-ghadah and al-maghrib, then wipes with three fingers thereof.

key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat
key_terms.بَاطِنِ: the inner side or inward surface
key_terms.ظَاهِرِ: the outer side or outward surface
key_terms.مَسْحِ: wiping, specifically the prescribed wiping in wudu

ai.seo_question: How should men and women perform the arm-washing and head-wiping in wudu (ablution) according to this hadith from Imam al-Rida عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report states a legal ruling on the manner of wudu (ablution), distinguishing between women and men in how the arms are washed. It also includes a juridical note permitting a woman, under certain circumstances, to wipe her head through or beneath her head-covering in specific prayers.
